data.name: Hertha
data.gender_notes: Hertha is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Goddess of fertility and motherly love
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old German words ‘heri’ (army) and ‘thu’ (goddess). In Norse mythology, Hertha was a goddess of fertility, protection, and motherly love. In Christianity, Hertha is associated with the Virgin Mary and revered as a patroness of mothers and children. The name Hertha carries the meaning “Goddess of fertility and motherly love” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Hertha usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of fertility and motherly love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the nurturing and protective nature of God and the motherly love of the Virgin Mary.
data.etymology: Hertha belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of fertility and motherly love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hertha total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: הריטה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: הריטה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשפה הגרמנית ופירושו אדמה או קרקע. השם קשור למושגים של יצירה, התחלה והקשר לאדמה. הוא משמש לעתים קרובות כסמל לחיבור לאדמה ולטבע.

in_greek.name: Χέρτα
in_greek.meaning: Χριστιανικό όνομα που σημαίνει γη, έδαφος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χέρτα είναι χριστιανικό και προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα, που σημαίνει γη ή έδαφος. Είναι ένα όνομα που συνδέεται με την έννοια της δημιουργίας και της αρχής, συμβολίζοντας τη σύνδεση με τη γη και τη φύση.

in_latin.name: Hertha
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Hertha is of Germanic origin, signifying earth or ground. It is associated with concepts of creation, beginnings, and connection to the land. Historically, it has been used in Christian traditions to symbolize a bond with the earth and nature.

in_english.name: Hertha
in_english.long_meaning: The name Hertha is derived from Germanic roots, meaning stronghold, earth, or ground. It symbolizes a connection to the land and nature, reflecting a strong and stable character. While not directly mentioned in the Bible, its etymology relates to biblical concepts of creation and the earth. Historically, the name has been used in various Christian cultures, signifying a deep-rooted spiritual connection.

data.cultural_impact: In pre-Christian Germanic cultures, the name Hertha was attributed to the goddess of womanhood, fertility, and protection. Post-Christianization, it evolved to signify devotion, motherhood, and unwavering support. The name maintains a significant connection to the legacy of Germanic mythology and the strong traditions of motherly love and protection.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, Hertha is revered as a patron saint of mothers and children. The name embodies the unwavering love, protection, and nurturing nature of the Virgin Mary, who is believed to intercede on behalf of those who pray to her. Therefore, Hertha, as a Christian name, serves as a constant reminder of the spiritual value of maternal love and loyalty. It exemplifies the deep reverence and connection between the Christian faith and the age-old tradition of the importance of motherhood.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hertha is a Germanic name meaning "bright, glorious one." It is associated with the goddess Hertha, who presided over springs, wells, and fertility. The name evokes images of purity, renewal, and the power of nature.
